$comment: Cross-SDK disagreements that are known, understood, and being worked. Every entry needs a reason and a hard expiry. NEW drift fails the run; an expired entry fails the run; and a recorded entry whose SDKs now AGREE also fails, because a note describing a state that no longer exists is the same rot as a stale finding. Baseline taken 2026-08-13 from the first three-SDK run (python, go, typescript). Nothing here is acceptable — it is the work list. 2026-08-13 later the same day: nine entries removed after the TypeScript int8 coercion, pathIn decode and datalog arity fixes landed — the runner refuses to keep an entry whose SDKs now agree. 2026-08-13, third pass: the four SQL/vector entries removed after the engine fixes landed — dimensionless-VECTOR row omission and the statement-Describe column typing. The three that remain are SDK-side work, not engine defects.

drift.reason: S22 decided the contract — get_path returns the VALUE — and landed it in Python only. Go (document.go PathIn) and TypeScript (pathIn) still return the engine's raw JSON text, so a string arrives as '"ada"'. Port the decode.

Three different answers to the same question. Python synthesizes raw point retrieval from 60 bucketed TS_RANGE_AVG calls. Go's TimeSeries.Query refuses outright with 'raw point retrieval is not supported by the engine' — which is false, since Python does it on the same primitives. TypeScript has no raw point read at all. Decide once whether the SDK owns this synthesis, then make all three agree.

Go and TypeScript both return CDC events as a raw JSON STRING rather than a list; Go has no CDCEvent type at all. Latent false green risk: a non-empty string is truthy, so a nonEmpty assertion would pass on an empty result.
